baer-heitev/1:_: To light. So too the Ari z"l. See Shlah that for Hanukkah one word; see in Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 3 whether if he forgot and lit one candle less than proper he should light more and not bless, for the blessing he made at the beginning was on the obligation of all the candles — Beit Yosef siman 672. Magen Avraham there.
baer-heitev/4:_: To the right. In Tur HaShulchan siman 106 he wrote that the people of the Rhine begin to kindle at the candle further left and turn toward the right because of "all corners," etc., and so did Maharam. The people of Austria begin on the right side and kindle as we — Bnei Brit — write; he wrote there to reconcile these views: where there is no mezuzah in the room, one must in any case kindle on the right of the entrance at the side of the tefach next to the door — and so the candle opposite his right is always next to the door and he must begin with it, for it is the essence of the mitzvah; by itself it suffices if he were not among the mehaderin. But the people of the Rhine speak where he has a mezuzah in his room — then he must kindle on the left of the entrance, and the candle next to the door is always opposite his left. If you ask: why then does Maharam need the reason of "all corners," etc.? — it could be resolved from the reason that one must begin with the tefach next to the door. One may say there is a difference if the candles were arranged from the side of the door toward the wall opposite the door — such as if the door is in the east and the candles are arranged from east to west, then he must turn his face south and begin with the candle next to the door and not turn north and begin with that candle because of "all corners," etc. — end. Beit Yosef wrote on this and it appears the custom of the people of the Rhine is correct, that one must kindle every night on the additional candle, as written here in Shulchan Aruch, and one should not distinguish between when the candles are on the right of the entrance and when on the left — and so we practice — end. {Rama: And here in Magen Avraham he wrote that Maharil and Mahariv speak when he eats in the room alone and it is not correct — see Eliyah Rabbah and it is explained in Bach and in Knesset HaGedolah that the participant must hear the blessings from the one who blesses, for otherwise he must bless on seeing.} And Rashal the meticulous wrote he should place them lengthwise on a spit so all are equal in the tefach next to the door, begin on the left and turn right — so too Bach. So too Taz: I practiced myself the most correct way to arrange the candles in length near the door as Rashal said so all candles are in the tefach next to the door; on the first night kindle the candle at the wall, on the second night add a second candle next to it toward the room's interior, begin with the additional candle and finish with the candle at the wall; on each subsequent night add one candle toward the room's interior, begin with it and finish with the one at the wall. If impossible to arrange thus, arrange them on the wall in a row from the right of the door — even if the others he adds are not all in the tefach next to the door there is no concern, since the first candle is in that tefach it suffices; each night begin with the additional candle which is the right available before the person and then kindle until the candle at the wall — as above, correct — end there. Machatzit HaShekel wrote in the name of Rashal to place them within the door's opening like the mezuzah — end there.
beer-hagolah/5:_: Mahariik in root 124 — see Mordechai in chapter 2 of Shabbat in the name of R' Meir
biur-halacha/5:ב: (ב) In order to turn to the right — see Mishna Berurah and the view of Levush and Taz that the Gemara's intent is the opposite of this, namely that one goes from right to left [and you saw Magen Avraham against this view was already rejected by the Acharonim — see Shaarei Teshuvah] — and per this Taz ruled thus: where there is a mezuzah and one must arrange them on the left of the entrance at the wall, arrange them in the tefach next to the door; on the first night place the candle at the door, on the second night place the additional candle toward the room's interior — the additional candle is on his right and the first on his left; he begins kindling from the additional candle and lights from right to left; on the third night when he adds another candle it is on his right and the first candles on his left — he begins from the additional candle and goes right to left. Where he arranges them in the door's opening or window or synagogue — on the first night at the row's end the candle is on his left; on the second night place the additional candle next to it on his right and the first remains on his left; he begins from the additional candle on his right and goes right to left; each night when he adds the additional candle he lights from it right to left until on the eighth night the additional candle is at the row's end on his right and he lights it first too and goes right to left — he must stand with his back to north and face south. See Peri Megadim who wrote he practiced like Taz — we have three views: Mechaber, Rashal, Gra, and Taz; each does per custom; even if Chayei Adam mentions only Shulchan Aruch and Maharshal, do not reject Taz after Peri Megadim and Dagul MeRevavah copied it to halacha; in any case for the mitzvah itself all agree l'chatchila only differs where to begin kindling.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [ד] And one does not kindle, etc. Bach wondered and ruled that even if one kindles in his house he must bless whoever does not hear the blessing — so Mordechai wrote — and Taz disagrees that Mordechai is alone against Tur and Ran, as Knesset HaGedolah and Magen Avraham ruled. I wonder: Bach wrote it follows Rif, Rambam, Rosh, Semag, and Agudah, and Rashal ruled so; I also found Keli Yakar and Shiltot Giborim daf 106 in the name of Riaz, and in Shiltot Giborim around Mordechai in the name of Ittur and Rashba, and in Rama's responsum siman 99 — no doubt if the great ones above had seen the poskim I brought they would not disagree with Bach. I also say Tur's view is likewise: he wrote one does not kindle for him and did not write "in his house" as in siman 677 — his intent excludes when he hears the blessings, for even if they do not kindle and he blesses himself he need not bless on seeing; what he wrote in siman 677 "if they kindle for him in his house" — no more is needed. It appears to me he need not kindle and need not participate as it speaks there, but he does require a blessing on seeing. Shulchan Aruch, Rama, and all the greats understood Tur that no blessing is needed and strained his words — in my humble opinion correct as I interpreted.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (ה) In the wording of the blessing she'asah nissim one says bayamim hahem bazman hazeh — so explained: He performed miracles in days that actually passed at this time, not as some say bayamim hahem uvezman hazeh. Rashal in responsum siman 64. Knesset HaGedolah there. Magen Avraham beginning of the section Farach. Eliyah Rabbah letter 1 Birkat Chayim letter 2 Ruach letter 3 Yafeh Lecha letter 4 Mishna Berurah letter 1:
magen-avraham/5:_: To turn to the right. So too Yoma daf 58 that this is called "the way of the right"; so too in responsum of Maharil siman 40:
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) To kindle a Hanukkah light — in Gemara and all poskim it is ner shel Chanukah; so Maharshal, but he wrote to say shelchanukah in one word and not shel Chanukah — two words. The world is not careful about this [Peri Megadim]. Bazman hazeh and not uvezman. We arrived at bazman hazeh — the lamed is chirik and not patach:
peri-megadim/2:_: Before ATZ — if he kindled all the candles he sees he should not bless afterward, for in all matters of a mitzvah without duration one does not bless afterward; the time of saying it is on the second night — not after kindling on the first night; when he remembers is on the third night onward, for these blessings were instituted only from kindling. Some say like festival that one says it even in the market — Pri Chadash here; Magen Avraham 673:1. However one may say she'asah nissim and shehecheyanu — the viewer also blesses them as in siman 15 here, even if he kindled all without blessing at kindling he blesses on seeing; but blessing to kindle — no, for it already passed. However if he kindled one candle one may say he blesses on the rest on night two onward even though the first is only the mitzvah and the rest are mehaderin — as siman 671; nevertheless Magen Avraham letter 1 in the name of Beit Yosef 673 wrote the blessing refers to all of them — it implies if he did not intend to bless he blesses on the rest; Eliyah Rabbah — it will be explained there. Nevertheless requires study, since after the mitzvah there is only mehaderin.
turei-zahav/5:_: He will begin to kindle, etc. In Tur HaShulchan siman 106 wrote the people of the Rhine begin at the candle further left and turn right because of all corners, etc., and so Maharam; the people of Austria begin on the right and kindle as Bnei Brit write; he wrote to reconcile these views: where there is no mezuzah in the room one must kindle on the right of the entrance at the tefach next to the door as Mordechai — and the candle opposite his right is always next to the door and he begins with it, essence of mitzvah; by itself suffices if not mehaderin. Rhine people speak where he has mezuzah — then left of entrance, candle next to door always opposite his left. If you ask why Maharam needs all corners — resolve from beginning at tefach next to door; one may say difference if candles arranged from door toward wall opposite — door east, candles east to west, turn south, begin candle next to door, not north — because of all corners — end. Beit Yosef wrote it appears Rhine custom is correct, kindle every night on additional candle as Shulchan Aruch, no distinction right or left of entrance — so we practice — end. Rashal the meticulous places lengthwise in tefach next to door so all equal near door opening; then kindle left to right, always begin leftmost and add rightward; in synagogue where menorah faces south, placed east-west, turn left to right — end. Levush wrote: I say the explanation of all corners is not as they explain but as our writing way, etc., as from encircling the altar the kohen ascended south and began southeast corner, etc.; if kohen could stand in place to throw — he is as said, etc.; he extended on human nature turning — so too here l'maaseh like Austria — end. It appears his words are correct: what Chazal said all corners means beginning the corner — you have right and left, whenever you begin turn right; first time with two or more before you, kindle the rightmost; if we explain kindle leftmost first to then turn right — why is the end preferable to the beginning which is primary? Rather certainly explain on the beginning: with two sides take the right, then go to its left; therefore I practiced arranging candles lengthwise near door as Rashal so all in tefach next to door (kindle first night at wall candle, second night add second toward room interior, begin additional, finish wall candle; each night add toward interior, begin additional on his right, finish wall candle; if impossible arrange on wall in row from right of door — even if later additions not all in tefach next to door no concern since first is in that tefach; each night begin additional on his right and kindle to wall candle — correct; in synagogue arranged menorah east-west kindle first night easternmost, add westward, always begin additional — end siman 671 regarding lulav). One more reason to begin at leftmost which is person's right — otherwise he passes over mitzvah moving hand toward candles before him when he could kindle left candle first then those before him — end, correct.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] To kindle a Hanukkah light. Thus is the main precise formula; the formula in Shas and Rif and Rambam in which it is written to kindle a ner shel Chanukah is not primary. Peri Chadash. Shaarei Teshuvah letter 2; so too Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 3 that it is better to bless lehadlik ner Chanukah and not shel; per the secret acronym nachal. Beit David letter 11 in Hagahot Taz. So too Yafeh Lecha part 2 letter 2, Ben Avraham parashat Vayeshev letter 2 — see there he wrote several reasons for this. Also see the letter after it.
peri-megadim/3:_: And it is not [before] ATZ. Rashi Shabbat 23a — one who has not yet kindled in his house, or one sitting on a ship — Avodat HaKodesh; and Taz explained the word "yet": one explanation; and possibly "yet" means all night even if he kindles on night two — [Rashi's] language is that he does not bless shehecheyanu on the first and blesses shehecheyanu on night two; it teaches us he blesses shehecheyanu immediately and on night two does not bless shehecheyanu. Requires study: if so, what of "or one sitting on a ship"?
shaarei-teshuvah/4:_: To the right. See Bach; and see in Pri Megadim part 1 section 98 who wrote on the proof of Magen Avraham from Yoma daf 59 that there is no proof — one may say it is fine as Levush to kindle from right to left as the way of writing; there too regarding gifts from the inner altar one may say that what draws his hands toward him as the way of writing is the way of the right, and what draws his hand away from his body and onward is the way of the left — see there.
